project_metadata.job_description: I am seeking a skilled freelancer to assist with writing and editing my resume and cover letter. The ideal candidate will have experience in crafting compelling job application materials that highlight key skills and experiences. Attention to detail and creativity in presentation are essential. The goal is to create documents that effectively communicate my strengths and enhance my chances of securing job interviews.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Marissa, thank you for the kind words—and especially for being candid about your budget. Knowing that upfront makes it much easier to identify the right fit.

Rather than billing hourly, I use flat project rates. Most clients find that approach more straightforward because the scope and total cost are clear before we begin, so there are no surprises.

My standard resume-and-cover-letter package starts at $275. It includes a thorough intake process focused on your background and goals, a fully ATS-optimized resume delivered in Word and PDF, a tailored cover letter, and 4 rounds of revisions so everything feels right to you.

Once I have everything I need from you, turnaround is generally 6-8 business days.

We can also discuss alternatives if the budget is tight right now. One option is to begin with the resume alone, then add the cover letter when you’re ready. Whichever route you choose, I want you to receive something that genuinely works for you.

What kind of timeline are you working with, and which types of roles do you plan to target?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: What I’m really asking is: what does "standard" include?

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Given the current hiring market, I’ve started creating two resume versions for many clients: a “Standard” edition and a “Signature” edition.

The baseline deliverables include a fully ATS-optimized resume supplied in Word and PDF, a tailored cover letter, and 4 rounds of revisions.

**Standard Edition**
Built primarily for function, this is a clean, professionally formatted resume that is ATS-compatible, easy to read, polished, and ready for recruiters. You receive both Word and PDF files, so you can make your own updates. It’s the best fit for online applications that may pass through automated screening before reaching a person.

**Signature Edition**
Along with everything included in the Standard edition, this option gives you a visually designed resume created in Canva and branded specifically to you. Its modern, eye-catching presentation works especially well when sending materials directly to a hiring manager, attending networking events, or displaying the resume in a portfolio. Clients often choose this tier when presentation is just as important as content because it stands apart from a traditional resume.

**Cover Letter**
Instead of a generic template, you receive a fully tailored narrative written in your voice and aligned with your target role. As with the resumes, I can prepare both standard and signature versions; the signature letter follows the design style established for the signature resume.

**LinkedIn Optimization**
Many clients add this service to their package as well. Rather than simply copying resume content onto a profile, I rewrite the headline, About section, and experience entries for visibility within LinkedIn's search algorithm so recruiters can find you. I also provide guidance on keywords, profile settings, and positioning for your target roles.

Where are you in the process right now—actively applying, or still working out your next move? And do you already have a budget in mind?

Presentation is the only distinction; the content itself does not change. Both versions receive the same research, strategy, writing process, and carefully developed bullet points.

For general applications, the Standard provides a clean, professional Word/PDF document that is functional, readable, and ATS-friendly.

With the Signature, that identical content is placed into a custom Canva design with tailored typography, layout, and visual branding. It’s meant to catch someone’s attention when it arrives in an inbox. Many clients keep both versions, using the Standard for online applications where ATS is involved and the Signature for networking or direct outreach where visual impact matters.

And yeah, neither resume version is connected to the LinkedIn add-on—that’s an entirely separate process lol. I definitely understand what you mean about social media, too; that’s another topic altogether, and it can certainly be detrimental.

I’m so glad we’ll be working together! While the contract is being sent over, it would help if you started gathering the following materials so we can begin quickly after it’s signed.

First, send your current resume if you have one. It can be outdated or rough; either way, it gives me a useful starting point. If no resume exists, that’s completely fine—we can build it from scratch.

Please also share any target job postings you’re considering. At a minimum, I’ll need the job titles and industries you want to pursue, and greater specificity will be more helpful.

**Background info:** Include a brief overview of your work history, major accomplishments, skills, and anything that distinguishes you. At this stage, rough notes or bullet points are perfectly acceptable.

There is no wrong format for sending any of this. A messy Word document, several paragraphs, or a loose list of previous jobs will all work for me. The more information you provide, the more effectively I can tell your professional story.

I’m looking forward to starting!

Hi Marissa,

It was great connecting with you! I’ve attached the intake questionnaire as promised; your responses will give me the information I need to develop a strong first draft.

Although the questionnaire may look lengthy, you don’t need to perfect every response. Rough thoughts, notes, bullet points, and even partial answers are all completely acceptable. More detail helps me tell your story more effectively, but incomplete responses still give me a solid place to begin.

Please give a little extra attention to these sections:
∙	Your current role — because you handle many different responsibilities, I want to ensure none of them are overlooked
∙	Your side work — that experience has more value than many people realize, so I want to frame it in a way that benefits you
∙	Your job target — even a broad direction allows me to tailor the document’s focus and language

After I receive the completed questionnaire, I’ll contact you with the timeline for your first draft.

If anything is unclear, feel free to reach out. We can also talk through any questions before you fill it out.

I’m looking forward to working with you!
- Darius

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi Marissa,

First drafts are ready for your review! I've attached the Standard and Signature editions of both the resume and cover letter, so four documents total.

Quick orientation on what you're looking at:

The **Standard editions** are your ATS-optimized Word and PDF versions, built to pass through automated screening systems for online applications. Clean, professional, easy for you to update yourself down the road.

The **Signature editions** are the designed Canva versions, branded to you and built to stand out when you're sending directly to a hiring manager, networking, or following up after a conversation. Same content, different presentation.

A few things to know as you read through:

Since your questionnaire had some open spots, I filled in a few gaps with educated guesses based on your old resume. The big ones are your timeline (Redwood Pathways as 2013 to 2020, your freelance executive support services as 2016 to 2024, and Cedarstone Collective from September 2023 forward), and the positioning, which I aimed at Administrative Operations/Office Manager roles since that's where your experience is strongest. I also cut Harbor & Finch since it's older than 12 years and didn't add to the story.

I've attached a short follow-up document with a handful of quick questions, mostly to confirm dates and pull out a few specific wins from your Cedarstone Collective role. Even a few words on each will let me sharpen the next draft considerably.

Take your time reading through everything. When you're ready, send back any edits, reactions, or answers to those questions and I'll fold them in. The first of the four included revision rounds starts here, so don't hold back; this is the time to tell me what feels right and what doesn't.

Looking forward to your thoughts!

Darius

messages.text:
Hi Marissa,

I'm so sorry, I had reviewed the answers but then at some point had it in my mind I was waiting for a response from you—my mistake! They were really helpful, and I've now updated both the resume and cover letter to reflect everything you shared. New versions are attached.

A few things to know about what changed:

The biggest shift is the overall positioning. Based on what you said about being open to something new and not necessarily targeting assistant roles, I rebuilt the resume around remote operations instead. The headline, summary, and core competencies now lead with operations, logistics, customer relations, and process building, which opens you up to a much wider set of remote roles (operations coordinator, customer operations, logistics coordinator, project coordinator, that kind of range) without losing the personal assistant experience, which is still in your work history. The cover letter follows the same direction and explicitly names the kinds of roles you are open to, so a hiring manager is not left guessing.

I also corrected the timeline: Redwood Pathways now shows 2013 to 2017, and your freelance executive support services shows 2014 to Present with a small "(Concurrent)" note so the overlap with Cedarstone Collective reads as intentional rather than confusing. Let me know if you would rather drop that label; it is completely optional.

Your Lakeview Design College qualification is now accurately shown (Associate of Science in Retail Management), and I leaned into your "built everything from the ground up" answer for Cedarstone Collective. That actually became one of the strongest parts of the resume; your builder mindset comes through really clearly.

If anything reads off—dates that need adjusting, language that does not sound like you, or anything missing—just let me know and I will fold it in.

Take your time; there is no rush.

Thank you,
Darius
